title: Nephi Grieves
summary: Nephi reflects on his brothers' hard hearts and on the destruction of his people that he had seen, and is overcome by affliction.

explicit_facts.text: Nephi's brothers did not understand their father's words and did not look to the Lord as they ought because of hard hearts.
Nephi grieves because of his brothers' hardness and what he has seen, which he knows will come to pass because of mankind's wickedness.

title: Nephi Rebukes Them
summary: Nephi asks why his brothers do not keep the Lord's commandments and reminds them that those who ask in faith without hardening their hearts will receive knowledge.

explicit_facts.text: Nephi questions his brothers about not keeping the Lord's commandments and warns about perishing because of hardness of heart.

title: The Olive Tree and Israel
summary: Nephi explains that the house of Israel was compared to an olive tree and describes the latter-day gospel coming to the Gentiles and then to his people's remnant.

explicit_facts.text: Nephi says the house of Israel was compared to an olive tree by the Spirit of the Lord in their father, and asks whether they are a branch of Israel broken off from the house.

Nephi explains that after the Messiah is manifested and his seed has dwindled in unbelief for many years and generations, the gospel will come to the Gentiles and from them to the remnant of his seed.

title: Judgment and the Kingdom
summary: Nephi explains that the vision represents temporal and spiritual things: people will be judged by their works, the unclean cannot enter God's kingdom, and the wicked are rejected from the righteous and the tree of life.

explicit_facts.text: Nephi says the vision represents temporal and spiritual things and that people will be judged by works done in their mortal probation.
Those who die in wickedness will be cast off spiritually and brought before God to be judged; the filthy cannot dwell in God's kingdom.

Nephi says a place of filthiness, hell, is prepared, and men's final state is to dwell in God's kingdom or be cast out because of justice.
Nephi says the wicked are rejected from the righteous and the tree of life, whose fruit is the greatest of God's gifts, and concludes speaking to his brothers.
